audit_title: NairaLLM — 105K Pretraining Compute Provenance & Execution Device Audit
executive_summary: Rigorous inspection of the execution telemetry, runtime task logs, serialized checkpoint files, and pretraining metadata proves unequivocally that the 25-epoch run was executed locally on the Windows workstation using the Pure-NumPy CPU Fallback Engine, and NOT on a Google Colab Tesla T4 cloud GPU. Although the code, notebook, and architecture for Colab T4 were prepared, the actual invocation was executed on the local host with '--allow-cpu-fallback'. No GPU was active.

1_host_platform.processor: Intel64 Family 6 Model 78 Stepping 3, GenuineIntel (4 threads)

3_execution_command_and_logs.log_hardware_gate: [HARDWARE GATE] RUNNING IN LOCAL CPU FALLBACK MODE: Host CPU (NumPy Engine / Fallback)
3_execution_command_and_logs.log_pytorch_status: PyTorch Status: Not Installed (NumPy Engine Active)

5_parameter_count_evidence.significance: 1,436,032 corresponds strictly to the Pure-NumPy untied embedding/output matrix allocation (193,152 * 2). If executed in PyTorch with CUDA, the tied parameter count would be 1,242,880.

provenance_reconciliation.recommendation: The local CPU run serves as a functional pipeline and weight convergence test. To perform the actual accelerated Tesla T4 cloud pretraining, open 'NairaLLM/training/cloud/nairallm_v1_5_free_gpu_pilot.ipynb' inside Google Colab with the T4 GPU runtime enabled.
